concept_html:
@pytest.mark.parametrize runs one test function once per row of a table. Each row becomes its own test, with its own pass or fail:

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("age", "expected"),
    [
        pytest.param(34, "16-34", id="below-35"),
        pytest.param(35, "35-54", id="at-35"),
        pytest.param(None, None, id="missing"),
    ],
)
def test_age_band(age: int | None, expected: str | None) -> None:
    assert age_band(age) == expected

pytest names each case from its values, such as test_share[1-4-0.25]. Give a case a name with pytest.param(..., id="missing"), so a failure reads test_age_band[missing].

Choose rows on purpose. For every threshold, test the value just below it, the value on it, and a missing value. Most banding bugs are a < that should be a <=.

Mark a known bug on one row with pytest.param(..., marks=pytest.mark.xfail(reason="bug #41", strict=True)). The row is expected to fail. With strict=True, the run fails as soon as the row starts passing, which tells you to remove the mark once the bug is fixed.

Two parametrize decorators on one test run every combination: two values times three values make six tests.

To run every test that uses a fixture once per value, give the fixture params. Read the current value from the built-in request fixture:

@pytest.fixture(params=["pandas", "polars"])
def backend(request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> str:
    return request.param

Keep the test body free of if statements that pick a behaviour per row. When some rows should raise and others return a value, write two tables and two tests.

solution_lines: def age_band(age: int | None) -> str | None:
"""Age group for reporting. None stays None."""
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
pytest.param(34, "16-34", id="below-35"),
pytest.param(35, "35-54", id="at-35"),
pytest.param(54, "35-54", id="below-55"),
pytest.param(55, "55+", id="at-55"),
pytest.param(None, None, id="missing"),
def test_age_band(age: int | None, expected: str | None) -> None:
assert age_band(age) == expected

title: Parametrize, one test and many readable cases
why_html: An age banding function had one test, for age 40. A refactor changed age < 35 to age <= 35, and every 35-year-old moved into the younger band. In a tracker with 800 respondents a wave, about 16 people moved band each wave. The 16-34 share rose by two points, and the client asked why. A parametrized test with rows 34 and 35 fails on that change before review.
